clue.text: One with much to say about milliner maybe at fight

blocks.note: c. (circa) is Latin shorthand for about
a hatter is one kind of milliner, hence 'maybe'
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A talkative hat-maker has plenty to say before a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is a person who talks incessantly, so someone with much to say.

clue.text: Fool, he's on drug — help to dry out here?

blocks.note: a clot is a British word for an idiot
taken as written
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A fool on drugs seems to need drying out, as in rehab.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the pieces run in order. 'Dry out' suggests addiction recovery, but it is laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a folding frame on which washing is hung to dry, so it assists drying; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Included in scam, ongoing

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the following words, so these words also tell us where to look

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone is caught up in a fraud that is still going on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles as the signal: the answer is included in the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be among a group is to be included in it, a straightforward prepositional synonym.

clue.text: Regularly stroke piggy

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to pet a pig often.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market' is counted on a child's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the children's rhyme each toe is a little piggy, so piggy is a playful name for a digit of the foot.

clue.text: Where to land in style after cricket score

indicators.note: after places one piece below the other in this down entry

blocks.note: a run is the basic unit of scoring in cricket
a way of doing something is a style

explanation.surface: Advice on making a stylish arrival after a big cricket score.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip on which aircraft touch down, the place for a plane to land.

clue.text: Timely pro, one put to work

indicators.note: putting letters to work sets them in motion so they come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A professional arrives just in time to put someone else to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune describes something happening at a convenient or well-chosen moment, the sense of timely.

clue.text: One not suitable if brought up in poor visibility

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from bottom to top
in places one piece inside another word

blocks.note: mist cuts down how far one can see
taken as written, before being turned upside down

explanation.surface: Someone is ruled unsuitable if raised in a fog of confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is a person who does not fit in, someone ill-suited to their surroundings.

clue.text: Easy to understand fury — red line's shifted

indicators.note: shifted means moved about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, with the S of the contraction

explanation.surface: Anger is easy to grasp when a red line has been moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something user-friendly is designed to be simple to operate or follow, so easy to understand.

clue.text: Gas from Australia, unique

blocks.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
one, as in one and only, is unique

explanation.surface: A singular gas comes from Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, a gas.

clue.text: Out of order, snap about family serviettes

indicators.note: something out of order is disarranged, so these letters must be rearranged
about means going around, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: the four letters reordered
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Faulty table linen gets snapped up around the family dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Serviette is the British word for a table napkin, so the two are plain synonyms.

clue.text: School having professorship and place for infant

indicators.note: having means one part comes with the next, joined end to end

blocks.note: a high school
a professor holds a chair at a university

explanation.surface: An academic post comes with a nursery seat attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A highchair is a tall seat with a tray where a baby sits to be fed.

clue.text: For example, Sparta, static, yet lively

indicators.note: lively letters jump around and so land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ancient Sparta is called static and yet lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was an independent Greek polis, a single city governing itself as a sovereign country.

clue.text: Distant fliers recalled

indicators.note: to call back is to send something the way it came

blocks.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Pilots far away are ordered home.
explanation.definitionFit: Far and distant both describe something a long way off; simple synonyms.

clue.text: View internet location, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the solver should listen for a word pronounced the same

blocks.note: a website is a place on the internet

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a web page that sounds right.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is something seen, such as a fine view or spectacle.

clue.text: Getting new start, traffic official, in this growth area?

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the neighbouring word
a new opening replaces the existing one of the official's title

blocks.note: its first letter
a traffic warden issues parking tickets in Britain

explanation.surface: A parking attendant tries a fresh career among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening W of the official is swapped for G, the first letter of 'Getting'. A traffic warden is a British parking enforcement officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a plot where plants are grown, so it is literally an area for growth.

clue.text: Absolute, say

blocks.note: first meaning: complete, total
second meaning: to speak or voice

explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like it introduces an example, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective meaning complete and a verb meaning to pronounce aloud.

clue.text: Some find odd learner's easy task

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the words that follow is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of find through odd into learner's

explanation.surface: Certain people think an unusual student's assignment is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddle is a British informal word for something very easy to do, a cinch.

clue.text: Pole on amazing roll initially

indicators.note: initially means taking the opening letter of each of the words

blocks.note: first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A Polish person is on a remarkable winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' tempts as a nationality, but it is a long rod.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is a long wooden shaft used to row a boat, a kind of pole.

clue.text: Perform well, embracing tricky role, in seaside area perhaps

indicators.note: something tricky is twisted about, so these letters are rearranged
embracing means holding something inside

blocks.note: to shine is to excel
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor excels in a difficult part at a beach resort show.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoreline is where land meets sea, which the seaside is an example of, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Returning US soldier meeting ladies, say, in house

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so read the word backwards
meeting means one part comes up against the next, joined end to end

blocks.note: GI is an American soldier
the ladies is a public lavatory, a loo

explanation.surface: A GI home from abroad meets some women in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dome-shaped dwelling built of snow blocks, a type of house.

clue.text: One supervising in street with energy — draw back

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
E is the symbol for energy in physics
taken as written, then read in reverse

explanation.surface: An overseer on the street energetically pulls back.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is someone who manages or oversees, for example at events or estates.

clue.text: Reliable, and thus top

blocks.note: so means thus or therefore
a lid is the top of a container

explanation.surface: Something is dependable and therefore first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid can mean dependable or sound, as in a solid performer.

clue.text: Concession for weak person

blocks.note: first meaning: something given to placate
second meaning: a feeble person, short for milksop

explanation.surface: A grudging allowance made for someone feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an appeasing gesture and, as in milksop, a spineless individual.

clue.text: Gym class referring to elected person, Conservative, as assertive

blocks.note: PE is physical education
re means concerning
an MP is an elected Member of Parliament
Tory is the common name for a UK Conservative

explanation.surface: A PE lesson about a Tory MP who is bossy.
explanation.definitionFit: Peremptory means insisting on immediate obedience, so forcefully assertive.
